title: Customer briefing: guided-replay option, SLA choice, and short statuspage copy
content:
Purpose: quick, customer-facing briefing template describing a new 'guided replay' remediation option we can offer customers plus clear statuspage phrasing and instructions for requesting SLA credits. This is a draft for CS -> customer outreach; intended to be short, actionable, and non-technical where possible.

Executive summary (one line): On 2029-09-11 we observed intermittent misrouted inference requests and cache evictions that resulted in duplicated or stale responses for a subset of tenant traffic; most traffic served normally. We are offering an optional guided replay to re-run affected requests for customers who need deterministic repro or rehydration, and a simplified SLA credit path for impacted tenants.

Suggested short statuspage updates (3 progressive posts):
- 2029-09-11 09:40 UTC — Partial degradation: Some requests in region us-west experienced inconsistent outputs; routing fallback triggered for a portion of traffic. Customers may see duplicate or stale responses in brief windows. We are investigating.
- 2029-09-11 11:10 UTC — Mitigation in progress: We deployed a safe routing rollback and non-destructive cache purge in affected fleets; ingress filtering reduced the occurrence of stale responses. Guided replay option being prepared for impacted customers.
- 2029-09-11 14:30 UTC — Recovery: Service restored to normal. Most requests are back to expected behavior. If you continue to see issues or need us to reprocess a set of requests, contact your CS rep (see below) to request a guided replay or SLA credit.

Who should read this: engineering/product leads and CS contacts at impacted tenants who: 1) rely on deterministic outputs for repro/audit, 2) ingest downstream stateful artifacts (e.g., embeddings or reranking) and need to reconcile, or 3) want to request a straightforward SLA credit.

Customer-facing technical summary (plain language):
- Root cause (short): A recent change to routing and cache eviction policies caused a small percentage of requests to be routed to nodes with older KV cache states. That produced duplicated outputs or older/partially updated results for the same input in short windows.
- Scope: ~0.8% of requests for tenants routed via our us-west fleet between 2029-09-11 09:25–11:00 UTC. Affected customers will typically see duplicate responses or responses that reflect brief state regressions.
- Data integrity: No customer content was exfiltrated or modified outside of the request/response lifecycle. We did not persist incorrect outputs into customer-managed storage.

What we did (plain):
- Immediately rolled back the routing change and applied a targeted cache reconciliation job to affected nodes.
- Added extra validation to the routing plane and increased KV cache consistency checks.
- Scoped a safe, non-destructive guided replay tool to re-run inputs on a known-good model state for customers who need it.

Guided replay option (customer-facing):
Purpose: reprocess a provided set of request ids/inputs against the recovered service state so customers can reconcile downstream systems or audit outputs. This is optional and offered as an assist — not automatic.
Prereqs we will need from customer: list of request IDs (or a time range + route), contact for secure data exchange, and a preferred window for replay.
What we will deliver: a CSV of input, original response, replayed response, and a short delta note if outputs differ. Replays are run with identical model/version settings and conservative concurrency to avoid rate impacts.
How to request (template to send to CS):
- Subject: Request guided replay — incident INF-3421
- Body: Please reprocess requests for tenant <TENANT-ID> for timeframe 2029-09-11 09:25–11:00 UTC. We will provide request_ids.csv and an S3 URI for secure upload. Contact: <Customer contact name and email>.
Estimated time to complete: 1–3 business days depending on request size; small batches (<=10k reqs) typically complete same day.

Self-serve remediation for customers (optional scripts we can share):
- If customers only want to revalidate small samples themselves, we can provide a sample curl + replay-helper script that will re-run inputs against the current hosted endpoint and label responses for manual reconciliation. Example snippet (customer can run locally):
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-v1","input":"<sample>","request_id":"<orig_id>"}'
(we will add a small helper that tags replays in our logs so we can correlate and assist if needed)

SLA credit path (simple customer copy):
- If you were materially impacted (duplicate/stale outputs that required you to rollback or reprocess), we will offer a credit equivalent to 5% of that month's usage for small impacts, or a custom credit for higher verified customer cost. To request credits: reply to your CS rep with a short summary and evidence (affected time range, estimated extra compute/engineering cost). We will triage within 5 business days.

Recommended CS talking points (bullet list):
- Acknowledge: we discovered routing/cache inconsistency and rolled back within ~1.5 hours.
- Reassure: we prioritized safe recovery and validated models on the control plane; no external data exposure.
- Offer: guided replay + self-serve scripts + straightforward SLA credit; prioritize customers with regulatory/audit needs.
- Next steps: we will schedule a short technical postmortem call with any customer that requests detailed architecture notes.

Internal timeline + quick technical notes (for internal CS/SE reference only):
- 2029-09-11 09:22 UTC — routing change deploy started (canary).
- 2029-09-11 09:25 UTC — first anomalous duplicate responses observed; spike correlated with canary.
- 2029-09-11 09:40 UTC — incident declared; on-call SRE + serving runtime engaged.
- 2029-09-11 10:05 UTC — routing rollback initiated; two hotfixes applied to reduce KV inconsistencies.
- 2029-09-11 11:00 UTC — targeted cache reconcile pass started against affected nodes.
- 2029-09-11 14:30 UTC — reconciliation complete; monitoring shows stable behavior.
Root cause high-level: an optimistic routing policy change reduced strict node affinity for latency gains; combined with a cache-eviction heuristic change it allowed a small fraction of requests to land on nodes with slightly older KV state during a short window. The invariant checks we rely on did not trip fast enough.
Mitigations applied: staging of stricter routing safety checks, faster cache-consistency probes, and an automated rollback trigger on detection of response variance across replicas.

FAQ (short):
Q: Do I need to do anything?
A: If you saw no downstream harm, no action required. If you need reconciliation, request the guided replay or use the small sample script.
Q: Will my billing be affected?
A: No unexpected billing charges will be applied; if you incurred extra processing or engineering effort because of the incident, request an SLA credit and we will evaluate.
Q: Is this likely to happen again?
A: We added a rollback trigger and stronger pre-deploy checks; risk is reduced and we will monitor for regressions.

Next steps for CS (internal checklist):
- Review copy with legal/security for regulated-customer wording (ASSIGNED: Maya).
- Approve short statuspage messages (ASSIGNED: Ethan).
- Prepare guided replay intake form + secure upload instructions (ASSIGNED: Devon).
- Draft personalized outreach for top-20 impacted tenants (2-hour template + optional technical addendum).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Exact SLA credit thresholds (finance/legal to finalize).
- Whether to expose a permanent 'replay' button in Console vs. manual CS execution (product decision).

Notes to self / CS shorthand:
- Keep public language non-technical, emphasize no external exposure and that we are offering reprocess assistance.
- Track any customer requests via JIRA INF-3421-:CS-<tenant>.

Attachment ideas (for final customer packet):
- concise one-pager timeline
- guided-replay intake form (S3 presigned upload guide)
- sample replay CSV template and replay script
- optional technical addendum for customers that request deep dive

End of draft. Please add edits inline; we will lock final copy after legal sign-off.
